'''Pieter Hendrik Schoute''' (21 January 1846, [[Wormerveer]] &ndash; 18 April 1913, [[Groningen (city)|Groningen]]) was a Dutch [[mathematician]] known for his work on [[regular polytope]]s and [[Euclidean geometry]].

He started his career as a civil engineer, but became a professor of mathematics at Groningen and published some thirty papers on [[polytope]]s between 1878 and his death in 1913.{{Sfn|Coxeter|1973|pp=234-235}} He collaborated with [[Alicia Boole Stott]] on describing the sections of the regular 4-polytopes.{{Sfn|Coxeter|1973|pp=258-259}}

In 1886, he became member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.dwc.knaw.nl/biografie/pmknaw/?pagetype=authorDetail&aId=PE00002887 |title=Pieter Hendrik Schoute (1846 - 1913) |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=30 July 2015}}</ref>
